chapter: Jelly Roll, Leonard Reed and Chicago mixed crowds
title: Battles of music and drummer Chinee
summary: He tells of winning cup contests and the drummer Chinee.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You ever have any battles of music down here? Shucks.
I won two cups out of three.

With who? I won one from Chris Kelley. That's up. Tuxedo beat me. And I won one from Rene. But me and Rene split even. I'll tell you how that come out. See my bunch gave me the cup the first time we played, and then Rene had a white bunch too you see, and they gave him the cup the next time, well he and him split even see. But I won Chris Kelley and I won one from Rene and I lose with their tuxedo. They had twelve pieces and we had six. I couldn't do nothing but lose that.
I'd really have the six myself.

I ain't that little boy what you hear I'm talking about now, on drums with me. He was tying it up then. Chani. Chani was a whopping good little drummer then. That boy could play some drum. But he just was always wild, you know. But he always listened to me. He got bad after I left, you know, after I cut out and left, then he turned out bad, you know. But I could tell him, I said, Chani, we're going up to Audubon to play tonight or something like that. I said, we're not going up there drinking. We're going to go up there and play music. That's all. Okay, well he comes and he's over the land. Never did be drunk when I asked. When he started getting drunk we all were drinking, you know. That's when he started drinking.
